steps.text: Onion (25/30 g) finely diced into the oil (4 g flat, rapeseed — hot pan), medium, 4 minutes.
Passata (80/100 g), 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp mustard, a dash of Worcestershire, a pinch of sugar (1 g). 3 minutes.
Kidney beans (75/85 g) in. 3 minutes more, mashing six or seven of them against the side to thicken it. This is baked beans, made properly and without the sugar.
Spinach (60/80 g) wilted in a second pan,
then the eggs (100/150 g — 2 / 3) fried in the rest of the oil (5/7 g, rapeseed).
Beans onto the toast, spinach, eggs over.

why: Mash a few of the beans. There is no starch and no sugar syrup in this doing the thickening, so the sauce has to get its body from the beans themselves — half a dozen crushed against the pan is the difference between a sauce and a puddle.
notes: D0-003: both oil uses (the onion sauté and the egg fry) are cooking uses — whole row renames olive_oil -> rapeseed_oil (9/11 g, unchanged grams), restated as 4 g flat at the first hob step plus 5/7 g remainder at the egg step (4+5=9 her, 4+7=11 him).

Genuinely two pans running at once — the original text explicitly calls out 'a second pan' for the spinach/eggs — so this breakfast gets track markup despite rule 2's general 'single-pan breakfasts stay sequential', since it is not single-pan. Critical path lands both tracks at clockStart 10, matching the card's 10-minute chip exactly.

Seasoning: 'a pinch of sugar' weighed at 1 g (both covers), matching the sibling Week A resolution of the same cross-file sugar id (see a-d2d, and _ingredients.B.json's sugar note). Macro impact negligible (~4 kcal/cover).
